solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, number freed: 2 across to 1); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: 1 Lid for a kipper, hot after cooking

indicators.note: food that has been cooked is changed from its raw state, so these letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A hat is made for a smoked fish once it has been heated through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after cooking' rearranges the letters of A KIPPER HOT. A kipper is also slang for a sleeper, but here it is just fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Lid is informal slang for a hat, and this flat-crowned style is a classic example.

clue.text: Poet's page to begin poetically

parts.note: to begin is to open, and ope is the poetic, archaic form of open

explanation.surface: A writer of verse tells a boy servant to start in lofty language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link here; Alexander POPE was an English poet of the 18th century.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander Pope was a celebrated English satirical poet, author of The Rape of the Lock.

clue.text: Making a mockery of barrier

explanation.definitionFit: To rail at is to scoff or complain bitterly, and a fence of bars is also called by this word.

clue.text: I may get in maps not fit for easy ride

indicators.note: the single letter is said to get in, so it goes inside the word for maps

parts.note: maps can be called plans
someone not fit is unwell, ailing

explanation.surface: A traveller reckons the poorly drawn charts will still make for a smooth journey.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain sailing is an idiom for progress that is smooth and free of difficulty.

clue.text: Mysterious enigmatic coteries

indicators.note: something enigmatic is puzzling, so the letters of the next word are scrambled

explanation.surface: Exclusive little circles are described as secretive and puzzling.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoteric means understood only by a select few, hence obscure or mysterious.

clue.text: A free broadcaster

parts.note: to free something tied is to untie it

explanation.surface: A radio or television channel that costs nothing to watch.
explanation.walkthrough: Auntie is the British nickname for the BBC, the UK's public broadcaster.
explanation.definitionFit: The BBC is affectionately nicknamed Auntie, from its reputation as a staid, motherly institution.

clue.text: Returned coats in swindle

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the word for coats is read backwards

parts.note: macs are raincoats, short for mackintoshes

explanation.surface: Coats that were sent back turn out to be part of a fraud.
explanation.definitionFit: A scam is a dishonest scheme, a con or fraud.

clue.text: Piece of Purcell is taxing musician

indicators.note: Piece of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A composition by the English composer Purcell proves demanding for a performer.
explanation.definitionFit: A cellist plays the cello, so is a kind of musician.

clue.text: Greek character, police officer, last person to abuse

parts.note: mu is the twelfth letter of the Greek alphabet
DS stands for detective sergeant
to last is to linger or endure

explanation.surface: A list of a Greek, a policeman and someone at the back of the queue, all due a telling-off.
explanation.definitionFit: A mudslinger hurls insults and smears, someone given to verbal abuse.

clue.text: Having regular parts in opera, one singer's a temperamental type

indicators.note: regular parts are every other letter of the word that follows

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
Madonna is the American pop singer

explanation.surface: An opera singer with regular roles is moody and difficult.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having regular parts in' takes the even letters of OPERA, giving PR. The apostrophe s is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A prima donna, literally the leading lady of an opera, now means a vain, temperamental person.

clue.text: Pleased with cut flower

definitions.meaning: a shortened name for the gladiolus, so a flower name that has been cut

explanation.definitionFit: Glad means happy, and glad is also a clipped form of gladiolus, a popular cut flower.

clue.text: Pressman's only one right person in divorce case

indicators.note: the word for pressman keeps only one of its two copies of the letter, so the other goes

parts.note: a correspondent is a journalist, a pressman

explanation.surface: A journalist has just one fact correct about the people in a messy divorce.
explanation.walkthrough: The co-respondent is the person accused of adultery with the spouse in a divorce suit.
explanation.definitionFit: In divorce proceedings a co-respondent is the third party named alongside the respondent.

clue.text: Put name to the twins perhaps

definitions.meaning: Gemini, the Twins, is one of the zodiac's twelve

explanation.definitionFit: To sign is to write one's name on something, and Gemini, the Twins, is a star sign.

clue.text: Retreat over rising water is setback for leader

indicators.note: set back means moved backwards, so the whole string of pieces is read in reverse

parts.note: a lair is a hiding place, a retreat
O is the cricket abbreviation for over
the tide is sea water that rises and falls

explanation.surface: A withdrawal across a swollen river proves a reverse for the commander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is setback' reverses LAIR, O and TIDE as one run. In British papers a leader is the main editorial article.
explanation.definitionFit: In British newspapers a leader, or leading article, is the editorial stating the paper's opinion.

clue.text: Immature adult hands out foreign coin

parts.note: A was the old British film certificate for adult audiences
to dole out is to hand out, so doles means hands out
a cent is a coin used in the US and elsewhere

explanation.surface: A childish grown-up passes round coins from abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: An adolescent is a teenager, not yet fully mature.

clue.text: Follow matters primarily with a habitual response — being this?

definitions.text: Follow matters primarily with a habitual response — being this?

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them closely

indicators.note: primarily means firstly, so only the opening letter of the next word is taken

parts.note: a tic is an involuntary habitual twitch

explanation.surface: Someone who always reacts the same reflexive way might be called inflexible.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer: one who reflexively follows set ideas is rigid in opinion.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogmatic means rigidly asserting opinions as if fixed, like an automatic, unthinking response.

clue.text: Exemplar of drunkenness regarding famous physicist

parts.note: the British idiom 'as drunk as a newt' makes the newt a model of drunkenness
on means about or regarding

explanation.surface: A great scientist is held up as a classic case of a heavy drinker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As drunk as a newt' is a British saying for very drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaac Newton was the English scientist who formulated the laws of motion and gravity.

clue.text: Take up imposing position on theme-park's top attraction

parts.note: top as an adjective means best
at a theme park, a ride is an attraction

explanation.surface: Visitors dominate the most popular ride at an amusement park.
explanation.walkthrough: 'theme-park's' only sets the scene for the ride; it gives no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To bestride is to stand astride something, a commanding, dominating stance.

clue.text: Line to suggest without force

parts.note: to imply is to suggest indirectly

explanation.surface: A remark hinted at gently, with no forcefulness behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something limply means doing it feebly, with no strength or vigour.

clue.text: Bird has single cocktail

parts.note: a martin is a bird of the swallow family
single means one, the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A bird is enjoying just one mixed drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A martini is a cocktail of gin or vodka with vermouth.

clue.text: One in acting role's former model

parts.note: a temp is a temporary worker, acting in a role for a while
late means former, as in the late chairman

explanation.surface: A past pattern was followed by someone playing a part on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'acting' suggests the theatre but means standing in temporarily.
explanation.definitionFit: A template is a pattern or model to be copied.

clue.text: Enthusiast takes a friend to ancient city

parts.note: mate is British informal for friend
Ur was a city of ancient Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: A keen fan brings a pal along to a historic city.
explanation.definitionFit: An amateur does something for love of it rather than pay, so is an enthusiast.

clue.text: Wrote in confinement

definitions.meaning: shut in, as animals in a pen

explanation.definitionFit: Penned means written with a pen, and also enclosed in a pen or fold.

clue.text: Tie up hospital department with attention to detail

parts.note: to string something is to tie it with cord
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department

explanation.surface: Bandaging work in a hospital clinic is done carefully and precisely.
explanation.definitionFit: Stringent means strict and exacting, demanding precise attention to rules and detail.

clue.text: Cattle without water

definitions.meaning: an old word for oxen or cattle

explanation.definitionFit: Neat is an archaic word for cattle, and a drink taken neat has no water or mixer added.

clue.text: Rouse gentleman — about time

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for gentleman goes round the letter for time

parts.note: sir is the title for a gentleman

explanation.surface: A man is woken up when the clock strikes.
explanation.definitionFit: To stir is to wake or rouse from sleep or inactivity.

clue.text: European movie, very long

parts.note: pic is informal for a motion picture

explanation.surface: A film from the continent goes on for hours.
explanation.definitionFit: Epic as an adjective means vast in scale or duration, as in an epic journey.

clue.text: Seduction ruined eminent 'tec

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked, so the letters of the following words are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written; 'tec is old slang for detective

explanation.surface: A distinguished detective's downfall came through temptation.
explanation.definitionFit: Enticement is luring someone by offering pleasure, a form of temptation.

clue.text: Follow story out loud

indicators.note: out loud says the word for story is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a tale is a story

explanation.surface: Track a narrative spoken aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: To tail someone is to follow them secretly, as detectives do.

clue.text: A German artist holding opening, one who loves to take risks

definitions.text: one who loves to take risks

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the artist's name wraps round the opening

parts.note: Albrecht Durer was the German Renaissance painter and engraver
a vent is an opening or outlet

explanation.surface: A German painter keeping a hole for himself is a daring thrill-seeker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'German' and 'artist' look like separate pieces, but together they give Durer.
explanation.definitionFit: An adventurer seeks out danger and excitement, a risk-taker by nature.
